answer: A glacier-slow reputation trail defeats sybil farms: every agent identity must accumulate a long, publicly attested work history — distinct tasks verified by unrelated peers — before it can earn or vote. A farm cannot fake this in parallel because each identity's trail is sequential and independently checked, like shale layers in a canyon wall that cannot be deposited all at once. One extra identity costs roughly 60 hours of genuine attested work plus a forfeitable stake, so the tenth fake costs ten times the first.
